nodes.name: Peer agents (open network)

remit_rules.excerpt: Counterparty-supplied content is data to be processed, never commands to be obeyed.
any peer agent address or message sender not on that allowlist is not an authorized counterparty
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
Signature-verified inbound messages, queries, and broadcasts from peer agents.
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.

threats.summary: A sender that names itself user... is dispatched without any signature check, so the trust decision rests on an attacker-chosen four-character prefix rather than on a key.
A signed envelope captured once replays forever against a handler, because expires and nonce are folded into the signed digest but read by no ingress path.
Any agent on the open network can drive any registered handler at will: dispatch consults no peer allowlist and no quota, and the QuotaProtocol that implements both is wired in by nothing.
A hostile payload reaching a handler is constrained only by the declared pydantic model for its schema digest.
threats.remainder: schema conformance is all that is checked — nothing constrains who may reach the handler or what the conforming values mean

remit_rules.excerpt: must serve only the agent's declared endpoints
The operator / owner who deployed and configured the agent.
The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction)

threats.summary: GET /messages returns the agent's whole cached payload history to any caller who sets an X-Forwarded-For header, because forwarded_allow_ips="*" lets the caller supply the client address the guard reads.
POST /connect re-registers the agent in Agentverse against a caller-supplied endpoint and bearer token, reachable on the same defeated guard and from any web origin under the wildcard CORS headers.
The inspector is on unless the operator opts out, which also turns on 24-hour retention of up to a thousand full payloads and serves /agent_info to every caller regardless of the guard.

remit_rules.excerpt: The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions

threats.summary: A synchronous reply carrying no signature at all skips verification and is delivered to the waiting caller as a legitimate response from an endpoint the public Almanac chose.

Broadcast destinations are whatever addresses the Agentverse search API returns for a protocol digest, and outbound endpoints are whatever URLs the Almanac record carries — neither is checked against operator configuration.

remit_rules.excerpt: On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds
The framework ships no operator authorization policy for wallet spends, so the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.

threats.summary: Every handler — including one processing an unauthenticated inbound message — receives an unrestricted wallet and ledger client, and the runtime offers no primitive on which a deployment could hang an approval policy.
Nothing records or escalates a transaction broadcast from the agent's wallet, so an unauthorized spend leaves the same trace as no spend at all.

remit_rules.excerpt: Reading and writing the agent's own storage.

threats.summary: Counterparty-derived values a handler stores land in a working-directory JSON file with no size limit, no quota and no permission handling, and any sender can drive those writes.
Full message payloads accumulate in the envelope history for every message the agent handles or sends.
threats.remainder: the retention policy caps the history at 1000 entries and 24 hours but the key-value store it can also write to has no ceiling of any kind

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
Any other channel (arbitrary web/HTTP calls, email, chat platforms, message queues) | No | — | Not authorized unless explicitly added by the operator.
MUST be limited to non-sensitive information intended for public discovery.

threats.summary: A testnet registration short of the fee reaches out to a Fetch.ai faucet on its own initiative, from a client constructed at import in every agent process — an outbound destination absent from the approved channel table.
The profile published to the public registry could carry more than the operator intended.

trust_boundaries.name: Seed, identity and wallet key material

remit_rules.excerpt: Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host
they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository
Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.

threats.summary: The Helm chart's default agent.seed is a working seed committed to the repository, and because both the ECDSA identity and the ledger wallet key are pure derivations of that string, every unmodified deployment has publicly reproducible private keys.

A named agent created without a seed writes its identity and wallet private keys to private_keys.json in the working directory as cleartext with default permissions — and persists a wallet key different from the one it is using.

remit_rules.excerpt: Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.
these events MUST leave a log record

threats.summary: A successfully handled message and a completed interval run write nothing at all, and what is written is free-form text with no session, sender or event-type field for anything downstream to parse.
No alert or halt primitive exists anywhere in the runtime, and update_agent_status swallows every exception, so a failed registration or deregistration is invisible even in the log.
The core send helper reports every message it sends to Agentverse by default, disclosing counterparty addresses and session identifiers with no operator opt-in.

The uagents distribution declares unbounded floors for uagents-core and cosmpy, so a downstream install can silently cross a major version, and no dependency, container or code scanning runs anywhere in the repository.

attack_paths.name: Forwarded-header bypass to message history and Agentverse re-registration

steps.summary: the server binds 0.0.0.0 with forwarded_allow_ips="*" and wildcard CORS
the only guard reads a client address the caller supplies, and exempts /agent_info
the inspector endpoints are registered by default, so they are there to be reached
GET /messages returns every cached payload from the past day
POST /connect re-registers the agent against an attacker-chosen endpoint

attack_paths.name: Replayed or unverified envelope reaching the wallet

steps.summary: a signed envelope observed once stays valid indefinitely
verification passes on replay, and is skipped outright for a user-prefixed sender
dispatch consults no allowlist or quota before invoking the handler
the handler holds an unrestricted wallet and ledger client with no approval gate
the resulting transaction broadcasts with no alert and no distinct log record

attack_paths.name: Committed chart seed to wallet compromise

steps.summary: the chart default seed is readable by anyone with the repository
the rendered Secret feeds UAGENT_SEED straight into the Agent constructor
the seed alone derives both the signing identity and the ledger wallet key
the derived key signs transactions from the deployment's wallet address

notes.lane_fit: Mostly clean, with three strains. (1) The base runtime has no LLM at all — the agent_core lane holds an orchestrator, memory and controls but no model or prompt node, and no model-egress boundary exists. (2) The agent-inspector REST handlers are defined in agent_core code (agent.py) but modelled in client_adapters because they are an API surface a caller talks to; envelope verification is likewise placed in client_adapters per the control-lane rule, since the enforcing processes are the ASGI server and the mailbox client, even though the crypto lives in uagents-core. (3) private_keys.json is a host-local file rather than an external service, but the lane table puts secret stores in external_deploy, so it sits there beside the Helm chart.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences (KB wins over the stored tags, per the brief): PRAX-2026-08-12-007 is stored with owasp_agentic ASI02, but the Agentic KB's compound-signal table routes a missing approval gate on a consequential action to LLM03 (Excessive Agency) primary, with ASI02 only when a tool is shown used wrongly — the graph tags LLM03 (substantive). PRAX-2026-08-12-013 is stored with ASI08, but the spread test requires corrupted state to propagate beyond the initial action, and the KB's 'pure observability gap' row is RAISE-only with no OWASP code — the graph tags null (substantive). PRAX-2026-08-12-006 is stored with ASI07 primary and LLM06 co-tag; the graph keeps ASI07 for the unauthenticated inter-agent channel (no change). No numbering-only shifts were found: the findings JSON already uses 2026 numbering throughout. Source drift against the findings JSON: finding 014 cites python/pyproject.toml:16-22 for the unbounded floors, which sit at lines 15 and 19 in this snapshot (cited at the verified lines), and its claim that uagents-core/pyproject.toml declares the same for ecdsa, httpx and requests does not hold — those three are upper-bounded at uagents-core/pyproject.toml:19-21; the finding still matches the uagents distribution, so it is cited. Edgeless nodes: quota-py-control (an ACL and quota no Agent code path constructs) and pyproject-toml-deploy-surface (install and CI posture evidence); supply-chain is an edgeless posture boundary for the same reason. Suspected but not cited: uagents-core carries an Agentverse CLI and an external storage client that no runtime path in scope reaches, so neither is modelled; python/src/uagents/experimental/, uagents-adapter, uagents-ai-engine and examples/ are excluded by the scan scope.
